title: Private only, yet not disapproved: sainted speakers, approved books, pastors fostering popular devotion
source_text: LXXIV. Caeterum ista quidem a privatis tantum Doctoribus dicuntur: nec sunt authoritate publica definita, verum ea Ecclesia Romana non improbari, non pauca nec levia manifestum faciunt. Et primo quidem hoc inde colligitur, quod qui durius sunt ea de re locuti, in Sanctorum numero habentur, ut Bernardinus Senensis, Antoninus, Alanus, Bonaventura. Non leve quoque hujus rei indicium est, quod libri in quibus talia leguntur, sunt plerique Doctorum atque Episcoporum approbatione muniti, imo nonnulli Pontificum ipsorum. Praesertim vero quod ista magno studio inserta sunt & diligenter inculcata libris qui in manus populi traduntur, & devotionis plebis fovendae destinati sunt, idque non prohibentibus, neque reclamantibus, sed potius aperte faventibus Episcopis, & reliquis Pastoribus.
pass_a_gloss: But those things indeed are said by private Doctors only: nor are they defined by public authority, yet not a few nor light things make it plain that the Roman Church does not disapprove them. And first indeed this is gathered from that, that those who have spoken more harshly on that matter are held in the number of the Saints, as Bernardinus of Siena, Antoninus, Alanus, Bonaventure. Not light also is an indication of this matter, that the books in which such things are read are for the most part fortified by the approbation of Doctors and Bishops, nay some even of the Pontiffs themselves. But especially that those things have been inserted with great zeal and diligently inculcated in books which are handed into the hands of the people and are destined for fostering the devotion of the plebs, and that with Bishops and the rest of the Pastors not prohibiting nor reclaiming, but rather openly favoring.
pass_b_english: These sayings are private, not conciliar definitions—yet Rome does not disapprove.
Evidence: the harshest speakers are canonized; books carry episcopal and even papal approbation; pastors foster them in popular devotion.
